the ‘radiosensitivity’, in terms of the number of ‘hits’ per cell required for inhibition of the synthetic process, was inversely proportional to the amount of label.

the ‘radiosensitivity’, as measured by the ‘radiosensitising factor’, was a direct function of the specific activity of the tracer used, the ‘radiosensing factor’ varying from 0.2 to 2.0, the lower value being obtained when high specific activity tracers were used.
the ‘radiosensitivity’, as measured by the ‘dose’ required to reduce the rate of synthesis by 50%, was a function of the ‘label’ concentration, the ‘dose-rate’ and the ‘time’ of exposure.
